verdict.rationale: SumUp's own docs describe Offline Transactions, a store-and-forward flow: merchants keep accepting card payments when connectivity is unavailable or unreliable, card data is cached securely on the device, and it is uploaded later for processing and authorization. That covers both parts of the story, but the evidence is a single first-party SDK doc page with little depth. missing for 10: details on offline limits and risk caveats (transaction caps, upload windows, decline handling after reconnect), which readers or integration paths (Reader SDK vs. SumUp app/Cloud API) support it, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a merchant-ops user, I can keep taking card payments when the internet drops, with transactions stored and forwarded when connectivity returns

citations.quote: In this store-and-forward flow, card data is captured and cached securely on the device, then uploaded later for processing and authorization.
Offline Transactions let merchants continue accepting card payments when internet connectivity is unavailable or unreliable.
